text:
Nadia: quick note — our JS quickstart demonstrates naive parallel pagination (12 concurrent requests) and a new customer hit repeated 429s + missing items. Repro is simple and I can share logs.

Evan: ack. is this the SDK paginate helper or the sample pattern?

Nadia: sample pattern plus SDK retries amplify it. SDK retries don't respect Retry-After by default and JS default concurrency is 12 whereas Python is 4. When several pages hit transient 429s the retries line up and we get a bigger burst.

Tasha: two quick fixes: (1) change samples to use limited concurrency (p-limit or p-queue) with default 4; (2) add a small opt-in TokenBucket + semaphore in JS SDK and honor Retry-After header.

Evan: also make paginate helper treat 429/401 during paginate as retryable and preserve page cursor until final failure. That will avoid skipping pages.

Nadia: I'll update sample README and the quickstart code snippet. Patch idea: show both safe parallel (p-limit) and streaming sequential examples.

ci-bot: pipeline queued for evan/sdk-js-rate-limiter (sha: e7a1c4)

Tasha: please add a small e2e with a mock server that returns 429 for first 2 attempts on odd pages and assert no items lost. Telemetry: emit sdk.page.retries label to help SRE detect client-side storms.

Evan: will do. will open PRs for sdk + samples and tag you both for review.
